title: WPSS/1404/2022 of VEERPAL SINGH Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
UKHC010104262022
2026:UHC:7487
1
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition Service Single No. 1404 of 2022
18 August, 2026
Veerpal Singh
--Petitioner
Versus
State Of Uttarakhand & others
--Respondents
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Presence:-
Mr. K.K. Tiwari, learned Counsel for the petitioner.
Mr. Maneesh Lohani, learned Brief Holder for the State.
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Hon'ble Pankaj Purohit, J. (Oral)
Present writ petition has been filed by
petitioner seeking a writ of certiorari to quash the
transfer order dated 08.07.2022 passed by respondent
no.3 (Annexure No.1 to the petition) whereby petitioner
has been transferred from District U.S. Nagar to District
Almora.
2. The facts of the case are that the petitioner,
Veerpal Singh, is serving as a Kurk Amin in the
Cooperative Department, Government of Uttarakhand.
He was appointed as Kurk Amin pursuant to the
Government Order dated 18.04.2011. His case is that the
post of Kurk Amin is a district-cadre post and, therefore,
he could not be transferred outside the district. Earlier,
the petitioner was transferred from Udham Singh Nagar
to Pithoragarh vide order dated 15.07.2017, which was
challenged before this Court in Writ Petition No. 2637
(S/S) of 2017. The said writ petition was dismissed vide
judgment dated 27.06.2022, and the Special Appeal
preferred there against was also dismissed on

UKHC010104262022
2026:UHC:7487
2
13.07.2022.Subsequently, pursuant to the annual
transfer exercise under the Uttarakhand Annual Transfer
for Public Servants Act, 2017, the petitioner was
transferred from Udham Singh Nagar to Almora vide
order dated 08.07.2022. Aggrieved thereby, the petitioner
has filed the present writ petition, contending, inter alia,
that the transfer is contrary to the applicable service
rules and has been passed by an incompetent authority.
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that
the impugned transfer order dated 08.07.2022 is
unsustainable, being contrary to the service conditions
governing the petitioner. It is contended that the post of
Kurk Amin is a district-cadre post, as specifically
declared by Government Order dated 12.12.2011, and
consequently the petitioner, having been appointed
against a district-cadre post in Udham Singh Nagar,
cannot be transferred outside the district. Such transfer,
it is argued, would materially alter the conditions of his
service.
4. It is further submitted by the learned counsel
for the petitioner that the impugned order has not been
passed by the competent appointing authority, namely,
the Registrar, Cooperative Societies, Uttarakhand.
According to the petitioner, the order has been issued by
respondent No.3, who lacks competence under the
Uttarakhand Sangrah Kurk Amin Service Rules, 2011.
The petitioner also contends that the provisions of the
Uttarakhand Annual Transfer for Public Servants Act,
2017 cannot be invoked so as to override the specific
service rules governing his post. It is argued that the
impugned transfer is contrary to the petitioner's

UKHC010104262022
2026:UHC:7487
3
legitimate service rights and has been effected without
properly considering the nature of his cadre and the
applicable statutory provisions
5. Learned counsel for the respondent submits
that the petitioner's claim that the post of Kurk Amin is a
non-transferable district-cadre post is misconceived, as
the Uttarakhand Sangrah Kurk Amin Service Rules, 2011
impose no such restriction. The Registrar, Cooperative
Societies, being the competent authority, is empowered to
reallocate Kurk Amins between districts in administrative
interest, and such reallocation was made vide order
dated 30.06.2017.
6. It is further submitted that the petitioner,
being a Group-C employee, is governed by the
Uttarakhand Annual Transfer for Public Servants Act,
2017. The impugned transfer was made on the
recommendation of the competent Transfer Committee
and approved by the Registrar, hence, the mere issuance
of the order by the Additional Registrar does not render it
incompetent. It is lastly contended that the petitioner's
earlier challenge to his transfer on substantially similar
grounds was dismissed by this Court on 27.06.2022, and
the Special Appeal was also dismissed on 13.07.2022.
The present writ petition, therefore, merits dismissal.
7. Having heard the learned counsel for the
parties and perused the material available on record, this
Court finds no ground warranting interference with the
impugned transfer order dated 08.07.2022. The
petitioner's principal contention that the post of Kurk
Amin is a non-transferable district-cadre post has
already been considered by this Court in Writ Petition

UKHC010104262022
2026:UHC:7487
4
No.2637 (S/S) of 2017, which was dismissed vide
judgment dated 27.06.2022, and the Special Appeal
preferred there against was also dismissed on
13.07.2022. The Division Bench unambiguously held
that 'the nature of duties performed of Kurk Amins is not
such that a Kurk Amin of one district cannot perform his
duties in another district'. No subsequent change in the
applicable service conditions has been brought on record.
8. The present transfer has been effected in
accordance with the Uttarakhand Annual Transfer for
Public Servants Act, 2017, on the recommendation of the
competent Transfer Committee and with the approval of
the Registrar, Cooperative Societies. The mere fact that
the transfer order was issued under the signature of the
Additional Registrar does not, in the facts of the present
case, render the same without jurisdiction. The petitioner
has also failed to establish any statutory violation, mala
fide or other circumstance warranting interference in
exercise of writ jurisdiction. The challenge, therefore, is
devoid of merit.
9. Accordingly, the writ petition is dismissed.
10. Pending application, if any, stands disposed of.
 (Pankaj Purohit, J.)
18.08.2026
Rdang
